boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented University of Houston rituals, events, symbols, and spirit practices.

cards.title: Build Fiesta City
cards.subtitle: Annual student-run spring festival
cards.notes: Attend the three-day campus festival for student variety shows, performances, carnival booths, concerts, and the cook-off; entry is free.
cards.short_summary: UH’s long-running western-themed campus festival began in 1939.
cards.evidence_claim: UH identifies Frontier Fiesta as its oldest and longest-standing programming tradition; it is a student-run three-day event founded in 1939.
cards.access_notes: The official FAQ says entry is free; selected activities and food may have prices.

cards.title: Wear Red on Friday
cards.subtitle: Weekly Cougar-pride practice
cards.notes: Join the weekly campus cue by wearing red on Friday; it is an easy, public way to take part without needing an event ticket.
cards.short_summary: A Friday wear-red ritual shared across the Cougar community.
cards.evidence_claim: UH states that every Friday is Cougar Red Friday and invites students, faculty, and staff to wear red as a campus tradition.
cards.source_title: Cougar Red Fridays: Sparking Spirit, Building Tradition
cards.access_notes: Wear red on Fridays; no registration or admission is indicated.

cards.title: Rub the Bronze Cougar Paw
cards.subtitle: Cullen Family Plaza and TDECU Stadium
cards.notes: Before a game, visit the bronze cougar statues in Cullen Family Plaza or the statue at TDECU Stadium Gate 2 and rub a paw for luck.
cards.short_summary: A game-day good-luck ritual centered on UH’s bronze cougar statues.
cards.evidence_claim: UH documents that fans rub the bronze cougar paws before big games and identifies statues in Cullen Family Plaza and at TDECU Stadium Gate 2.
cards.access_notes: The practice is described for game days and before big games; follow venue access rules.

cards.title: Make the Cougar Sign
cards.subtitle: UH game-day hand signal
cards.notes: At a sporting event, fold the ring finger and thumb of your right hand toward the palm to make UH’s Cougar sign with the crowd.
cards.short_summary: A pride gesture rooted in the 1953 Shasta I incident.
cards.evidence_claim: UH says the Cougar sign is made by folding the right ring finger and thumb toward the palm and dates its adoption as a pride symbol to 1953.
cards.access_notes: Use it as a spectator gesture at UH sporting events or spirit gatherings.

cards.title: Have Shasta Bless the Rings
cards.subtitle: Biannual UH Ring Ceremony ritual
cards.notes: If receiving a class ring, look for the fall or spring Ring Ceremony: UH says rings spend the prior night with Shasta VII at the Houston Zoo.
cards.short_summary: A class-ring ceremony preceded by an overnight visit with Shasta VII.
cards.evidence_claim: UH documents that, before each biannual Ring Ceremony, class rings spend the night with live mascot Shasta VII at the Houston Zoo.
cards.access_notes: This occurs in connection with the fall and spring Ring Ceremonies; ring eligibility and purchase details are not stated on this page.

cards.title: Turn the Ring Inward, Then Outward
cards.subtitle: Student-to-alumni class-ring custom
cards.notes: If you own a UH class ring, wear its design facing inward while enrolled; turn it outward after becoming an alum, following the stated custom.
cards.short_summary: A wearable transition ritual tied to graduation and alumni status.
cards.evidence_claim: UH’s parent guide states that current students wear the UH class ring facing inward, while alumni wear it facing outward.
cards.access_notes: Applies to people who have a UH class ring; acquiring a ring may require purchase.

cards.title: Answer “Coogs House!”
cards.subtitle: UH athletics call-and-response chant
cards.notes: Listen for “Whose House?” at a Cougar sporting event and answer “Coogs House!” as part of the established athletics cheer.
cards.short_summary: A UH sports chant credited to a former cheerleader in 1988.
cards.evidence_claim: UH says “Whose House? Coogs House!” began during the 1988 football season and remains a staple cheer at Cougar sporting events.
cards.access_notes: Participate when the chant is led at a Cougar sporting event.

cards.title: Count Shasta’s Score Push-Ups
cards.subtitle: Football-game mascot routine
cards.notes: At a UH football game, watch Shasta and Sasha perform push-ups for points scored, then count along from the stands with fellow fans.
cards.short_summary: The mascot’s on-field push-ups turn the scoreboard into a spirit routine.
cards.evidence_claim: UH states that Shasta and Sasha perform push-ups for each point scored during football games.
cards.access_notes: This routine is described for football games; stadium ticketing and entry rules apply.

cards.title: Decorate for the Spirit Bell
cards.subtitle: Annual faculty-and-staff Homecoming contest
cards.notes: During Homecoming Week, eligible faculty and staff can enter by decorating an office around Cougar spirit for judging by the alumni association.
cards.short_summary: An office-decoration contest that extends Homecoming beyond the stadium.
cards.evidence_claim: UH describes the Homecoming Spirit Bell Competition as an annual faculty-and-staff contest recognizing offices decorated with Cougar spirit.
cards.access_notes: UH specifies participation for faculty and staff during Homecoming Week; judging details are provided by UH.

cards.title: Spot the Frontiersmen’s Flags
cards.subtitle: Cowboy-clad UH spirit organization
cards.notes: At football games, look for the Frontiersmen displaying the Texas and UH flags; their campus spirit role has continued for decades.
cards.short_summary: A long-running student spirit group with a recognizable game-day role.
cards.evidence_claim: UH states that the Frontiersmen have promoted Cougar spirit for 75 years and display the Texas and UH flags during football games.
cards.access_notes: Observe at UH football games and other listed campus or community appearances; event entry rules apply.
